answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a harbor as the anchor of the cost.
